subject: Stepped Concurrency Attenuation Profile — RFI for Performance Characterization
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Perf Team <perf-team@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: RFI: stepped concurrency attenuation profile (info requested)

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this RFI. To finalize our technical evaluation we need a focused dataset describing Redwood's behavior when traffic increases in discrete steps (what we're calling a "stepped concurrency attenuation" test). Please provide the following for the model variants you plan to test (name and engine/config):

- Test matrix: step sizes (e.g., baseline -> 2x -> 5x -> 10x), duration at each step, and inter-step ramp time.
- For each step: p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 token-generation latencies, per-request end-to-end latency, and aggregate QPS.
- Error/failure modes: increased timeouts, 5xx rates, rejected requests; include error taxonomy and counts.
- Resource signals during test: GPU util, memory pressure, queue depth, KV cache hit rate, batching stats (avg batch size, batch latency).
- Warm/cold start differentiation: evidence of cold-start latencies or significant cache priming effects.
- Behavior under contention: what fallback policies fire (model variant routing, region fallback, degrade to smaller model) and how quickly.

Additional asks: please attach the test harness or a runnable script (or notes to reproduce in our environment), and provide raw CSV/JSON artifacts and a short executive summary (1 page). Our evaluation deadline is Oct 21 — can you commit to delivering artifacts by Oct 15?

Attachments: none on this message.

Thanks,
Samir Patel
Perf Lead — Acme Corp

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: stepped concurrency attenuation profile (info requested)

Samir —

Appreciate the clarity. We can deliver the artifacts you requested. Quick outline of what we'll provide and our proposed test semantics so we're aligned before we run anything against your baseline: 

1) Test matrix (attached as stepped_concurrency_matrix.csv) — default step set: 1x (baseline), 2x, 4x, 8x sustained; step duration 15 minutes (initial), then 60 minutes for soak steps, inter-step ramp 30s–2m (configurable). We will also include a slow-ramp variant (linear increase over 10 minutes) if you want to compare impulsive vs gradual ramps.

2) Metrics captured — per-token latency histogram (1ms bins up to 5s), per-request end-to-end, token throughput, GPU utilization, CPU steal, queue depth, batch size distribution, KV cache hit ratio, and model-level stalls. We'll compute p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 and also include 99.99 if observed.

3) Error taxonomy — we will tag and count: request timeouts, admission rejects (overload), model OOMs, transport errors, and internal 5xx. Each will be reported with counts and example traces.

4) Cold vs warm — two runs: (a) cold start run with VM/GPU pools cycled between steps and with empty KVCaches, (b) warmed run with 30-minute pre-warm and sustained traffic before stepping. This will highlight priming effects.

5) Fallbacks and graceful degradation — we'll document which routing/fallback policies we exercised and instrument the timing when failovers occur. For Dedicated tests we'll show replica activation latency and for Hosted tests we'll show cross-model routing events.

6) Repro artifacts — we'll hand over: the load generator config (Locust/ghz-like YAML), the raw CSVs, Jenkins job IDs for our internal runs, and a short runbook to reproduce on your infra.

Timeline: we can start runs on Oct 9 and deliver a first artifacts bundle by Oct 14; final cleaned deliverable by Oct 15 if no scope changes. Sound good?

Attachments: stepped_concurrency_matrix.csv (text/csv), endpoint_config_snapshot.yaml (text/yaml)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Perf Team <perf-team@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: stepped concurrency attenuation profile (info requested)

Marcus —

That plan works. A couple of clarifications before you start: 

- Please include a 6-hour soak at 3x (steady) to check for slow memory leaks and warming effects.
- Provide the exact warmup script and seed corpus so we can mirror the priming.
- For graceful degradation, include timestamps for policy triggers and a short note on customer-visible impact (e.g., increased latency vs partial responses).
- Can you mark any artifacts that contain PII or customer data so we can handle them through our procurement/legal channels?

Confirming Oct 15 final deliverable is acceptable — we'll schedule an internal review Oct 18.

Attachments: none.

Thanks — Samir

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: stepped concurrency attenuation profile (info requested)

Samir / Marcus —

Looping in to confirm execution plan from Redwood side. Rishi and I will run the Dedicated cluster experiments you requested. Implementation notes and schedule:

- Runbook: we will run cold-run, warmed-run, stepped-run and a 6-hour soak at 3x as requested. The exact warmup script and seed corpus will be shared in the Drive folder (see link).
- Canary/fallback testing: we will stage a canary with traffic mirroring and then enable route-fallthrough to smaller model variants to observe customer impact. We'll capture per-request traces for any degraded paths.
- Data handling: any logs with customer identifiers will be redacted; artifacts with potential PII will be clearly labeled and delivered via secure Drive share or SFTP.
- Deliverable cadence: initial raw CSVs and a short executive summary will be uploaded Oct 14 (internal ID: RUN-20261009-1). Cleaned package by Oct 15.
